Improve key security isolation and prevent node workload stalls from freezing the GUI

result.summary: This pull request implements the core multiprocess separation architecture for Bitcoin Core, introducing an --enable-multiprocess build option that produces separate bitcoin-node, bitcoin-wallet, and bitcoin-gui binaries. The GUI and wallet processes communicate with the node over socketpairs using Cap'n Proto IPC wrappers around internal interfaces. It also updates btcsignals to destroy callbacks eagerly on disconnect, preventing proxy lifetime leaks from hanging process termination.
result.problem: Running the node, wallet, and GUI within a single monolithic process means that GUI responsiveness suffers during heavy node operations, and wallet keys share an address space with network-facing code. Isolating these subsystems into separate processes improves security isolation and GUI reliability.

resolved_concerns: Handling debug logs across multiple processes was solved by adding process-specific log suffixes (.wallet, .gui) and updating combine_logs.py
Race conditions and hangs during GUI shutdown were resolved by fixing btcsignals callback destruction timing on disconnect
Platform compatibility across macOS, NetBSD, and Windows was addressed with compiler attribute suppressions and atomic fallback handling

categories.evidence: Changes btcsignals to destroy slot callbacks eagerly upon disconnect and provides atomic shared_ptr fallback implementations.
categories.rationale: Fixes an issue where disconnected btcsignals callbacks lived indefinitely until garbage collection by a later connect() call. In multiprocess GUI operation, lingering callbacks holding IPC proxies caused bitcoin-node to hang on exit until test timeouts.

categories.name: wallet
categories.evidence: Implements interfaces::Wallet Cap'n Proto wrappers, creates the bitcoin-wallet executable spawn logic, and adjusts WalletLoader::restoreWallet parameter order.
categories.rationale: Enables privilege separation by running wallet code and keys in an independent process away from the p2p network daemon, although core wallet logic remains unchanged.

result.card: This PR implements multiprocess separation for Bitcoin Core, allowing bitcoin-node, bitcoin-wallet, and bitcoin-gui to run as separate executables communicating over IPC via Cap'n Proto socketpairs. It aims to improve key isolation by isolating wallet memory from network code and to keep the GUI responsive during heavy node operations. The change has strong concept support from maintainers and contributors, though an early concept objection is noted in the history. It is based directly on #29409, which should be reviewed first.
